newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil fiscal situation seen worsening numerically.
newsitem.headline: Brazil fiscal situation seen worsening numerically.

text.p: Brazil's fiscal situation is expected to worsen in March in numerical terms but not in real terms, a Central Bank official said.

Altamir Lopes, head of the bank's economics department, said 12-month figures would not include March 1996, an exceptionally good fiscal month because of one-time payments of corporate income tax last year.
"Probably in March we won't see such an accentuated improvement (in the public sector fiscal performance) in 12-month terms because you're taking out an exceptional month," Lopes said.
"Probably we shall see a slight worsening but with the prospects of continued improvement later," he added.
Brazil's operational public sector deficit in February reached 3.44 percent of gross domestic product, down from 3.68 percent of GDP in January and 5.08 percent in February 1996.
"We are seeing a pronounced tendency towards improvement month by month," Lopes said.

In March 1996, one-time corporate tax payments after adjustments on tax due helped the federal government post a 0.68 percent primary surplus after a 0.49 percent surplus in February and a 0.21 percent surplus in January.
The federal government's primary result, which unlike the operational result does not include debt servicing, slumped back to a 0.06 percent surplus in April 1996.
This year, payments on adjustments to tax bills were allowed to be divided into four installments, hurting monthly federal tax receipts.
In March, federal tax revenue was 9.388 billion reais, 8.2 percent down in nominal terms from the same month last year.
In February this year, the federal government posted a 0.39 percent primary surplus and in January a 0.3 percent surplus.
Lopes said continuing monthly improvement in the public sector operational deficit reflected better primary results because of spending controls and lower interest payments.
Real public sector interest payments were 3.47 percent of GDP in February versus 3.67 percent of GDP in January and 5.3 percent in February last year.

The Public Sector Borrowing Requirement (PSBR) was 45.944 billion reais or 5.75 percent of GDP in February. In the prior month it was 46.533 billion reais or 5.88 percent of GDP and in February 1996 it was 51.71 billion reais or 7.33 percent.
